newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Centertel to bid in digital phones tender.
newsitem.headline: Polish Centertel to bid in digital phones tender.

text.p: Polish cellular telephone firm Centertel, in which France Telecom has a 34 percent stake, is likely to bid in a coming tender to build a mobile phone network using the DCS 1800 system, its official said on Tuesday.

"Our company is ready to take part in this tender...and we are likely to bid in the tender after we undergo some structural changes," Centertel's deputy general director Krystyn Antczak told a news conference.
Last month, Telecommunications Minister Andrzej Zielinski said he expected to announce the tender in January.
Centertel, in which Poland's telecom monopoly TPSA holds a 66 percent stake, did not participate in last year's tender to run two modern digital GSM telephone networks.

It failed to join the tender because of rifts among its shareholders. As a result of the discrepancies over power and profit sharing, Ameritech Corp sold its 24.5 stake in Centertel late last year to the two other shareholders.
The company, which operates an older analogue NMT 450 system, now faces tough competition from two GSM companies, which lauchned operations in October last year.

Centertel still leads the market with more than 150,000 customers but its competitors, Era GSM and GSM Plus, are catching up. The company announced a price cut and a launch of new services on Tuesday to attract more customers.
